reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes EazyBot as a passive-income opportunity, presents recurring bot-profit figures, and directs viewers to register or test it through a linked destination while disclosing an affiliate relationship. The promoted material includes cryptocurrency performance figures, an “Add Funds To Wallet” control, and theoretical results based on a $1,000 starting investment. Risk disclaimers acknowledge possible total loss and that past performance is not a reliable guide to the future, but the affiliate registration solicitation remains.

citations.quote: Eazybot is better than crypto! Passive income simply in your sleep!
EazyBot registration (*) https://my.eazybot.com/159297
Again and again I see that easybot makes a profit for me week by week day by day Today almost 30 dollars again
If you want to test it yourself, you can find the link in the description

opening.argument: Judge, read the profit comparisons alongside the creator's express limits on what viewers should infer. The description says past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results and warns that cryptocurrency can cause a total loss of capital. The speaker likewise calls the investment volatile and risky. Those warnings make the figures a discussion of past performance, not a promise that viewers will earn the same returns.

citations.quote: The performance of all products in the past does not constitute a reliable indicator of future development.
The action with cryptocurrencies is risky and can lead to a total loss of capital.
you are doing all this in the crypto industry but that is of course a volatile and risky investment.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies enthusiastic language, reported profits, an affiliate link and an invitation to test the bot. Those establish promotion, but they do not establish a guaranteed return or concealment of the commercial relationship. The description expressly calls the marked links affiliate advertising, while the speaker acknowledges the risk of the investment. A registration invitation does not erase those qualifications.

citations.quote: The content (on the left) marked with (*) is affiliate (advertising) on ​​the left that support me in my investments on the respective platforms.
you are doing all this in the crypto industry but that is of course a volatile and risky investment.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk warnings do not change the central pitch. The description calls EazyBot a way to earn passive income in one's sleep, and the speaker directs viewers who want to test it to the link. The warning may qualify the expected outcome, but it does not turn the bot-profit promotion and registration invitation into neutral market commentary.

opening.argument: Judge, the substance is a worked comparison of a trading tool with buying and holding coins. The speaker poses the question of whether using a robot is worth the increased trading risk, explains why bot start dates must be accounted for, and even identifies a case where buying and holding performed substantially better. That willingness to show a counterexample supports reading the video as a demonstration of a comparison method, rather than a one-way earnings pitch.

citations.quote: Is it worth making a transition here? And increasing the risk of trading by a trading robot. Or is it better to just buy and keep.
because not all bots were started at the same time.
for Polygon, the bot performance here was 36,05% The Buy and Hold result is plus 98,30.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes the profit display, the funding control and the test link. A displayed control does not show that a viewer funded a wallet. Nor are the comparisons presented as uniformly favorable to the bot: the speaker says buying and holding Polygon made substantially more. Those details matter when deciding whether the presentation is primarily an examination of results or an unqualified solicitation.

citations.quote: We almost doubled up with buy and hold and made a total of 630 dollars more than with the bot trading.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A comparison can still serve a sales pitch. After presenting the results, the speaker says the bot made nearly twice the profit of the alternative and invites viewers to test it through the description link. The Polygon counterexample and the absence of a completed deposit do not negate that overall promotional direction.

citations.quote: we would have made profit on the stand today with both strategies, but nearly twice with our bot, which is very very strong.
If you want to test it yourself, you can find the link in the description

opening.argument: Judge, the observable transaction here is an openly disclosed referral to a trading service, not proof of a deceptive transfer. The description identifies the marked links as affiliate advertising and says using them adds no cost to the viewer. The invitation is to test the service; the cited invitation does not demand credentials, claim guaranteed returns or document a completed deposit. Treating the presence of a registration link and a funding control as proof of those further steps goes beyond what is shown.

citations.quote: The content (on the left) marked with (*) is affiliate (advertising) on ​​the left that support me in my investments on the respective platforms. This does not result in any additional costs, but you support me with it.
If you want to test it yourself, you can find the link in the description

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening is right that the creator advertises a bot and reports returns. But its cited registration link establishes a referral, not a completed payment or credential handoff. Its funding-control image likewise shows an available interface action, not that anyone took it. The explicit affiliate disclosure gives the judge a concrete commercial explanation for the link without requiring an inferred hidden transaction.

citations.quote: EazyBot registration (*) https://my.eazybot.com/159297
The content (on the left) marked with (*) is affiliate (advertising) on ​​the left that support me in my investments on the respective platforms.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed deposit is not necessary to assess what the video promotes. The creator pairs a bot registration link with a passive-income claim, repeatedly reported profits and an invitation to test the service. Disclosing the affiliate relationship explains the incentive; it does not remove the solicitation built around trading-bot returns.
